summary: Rows 139-144 are the opening of the manga's 羅将ヒョウ編 (the Rasho Hyoh block of the Land of Asura arc) and they adapt ch 188-195 in running order at ~1.4 chapters per episode — the slowest stretch of HnK2, because the first two rows are half anime-original. Ep 139 opens on ch 188 (Hyoh's 'merciless reunion' with the brother he does not recognise; Shachi gouges out his own eye), handing off from ep 138, which closes on ch 187; ep 144 ends inside ch 196's opening bedroom pages and ep 145 resumes there. Two type findings: eps 139 and 140 are NOT plain canon — hokutosite says of each that everything outside two named scenes is 'ほぼアニメオリジナル', and the fandom + hokutosite character indexes independently prove the padding is invented (Sayaka is ch 189 ONLY yet appears in eps 139-140; Kuroyasha's manga debut is ch 192 yet he appears in ep 139; Cain and Coyote exist only in ep 140) — both are mixed under T28, and both still carry real first-time source pages, so both keep an anchor. Two reorder findings: ep 140 plays ch 190's opening (Kenshiro's revival and the reversed waterfall) BEFORE ch 189's murder of Sayaka, and ep 141 opens on ch 189's held-back closing scene (Hyoh finding Sayaka's body and being told Kenshiro killed her) before finishing ch 190 — so eps 140 and 141 both END on 190 and both START on 189. Eps 141-144 are canon with heavy anime embellishment of manga scenes (Gyoko survives to die at the funeral, Petero and the Nagato flashbacks, the guillotine deaths cut); ep 144 'follows the manga almost identically' (RQ87).

Gyoko's whole sequence is restaged: the manga has his train reach Kenshiro's hiding place and Kenshiro tear his arms off and impale him, sending his men back with the message; the anime has the train plough into a village, Kenshiro stop it barehanded, and Gyoko survive to carry the message himself into Sayaka's funeral, where Hyoh's matouki destroys him. Ch 191's spine is intact but padded on both ends: the five retainers' despair, Nagato's flashback to the day he chose to follow Hyoh, and Kenshiro and Shachi being taken into Nagato's house are anime additions; Nagato's father Petero is invented; Hyoh cuts Nagato in half instead of beheading him; and Yom survives where the manga kills him. type_corrections.note: T28. Stored canon, AFL canon. The source half is real and load-bearing — ch 188 entire, the encounter the episode is titled for — but the other half is an invented plot: Lin's flight through the castle sewers and her sheltering by Sayaka (hokuto.fandom and hokutosite both index Sayaka as a MANGA ch-189-only character, so every frame of her here is anime-original), the checkpoint battle, and Kuroyasha's rescue eighteen episodes before his manga debut in ch 192 (both indexes: 'Anime (ep. 139, 143-150)' against 'Manga (ch. 192-209)'). hokutosite states it outright: everything but the jeweller scene and the eye scene is 'ã»ã¼ã‚¢ãƒ‹ãƒ¡ã‚ªãƒªã‚¸ãƒŠãƒ«'. Source + non-source in one episode = mixed; the row keeps its anchor (188).

structure.notes: FENCE AND HANDOFF. The outer fence is ep 108 -> 136 [135] and ep 152 -> 210; my six ENDs run 188, 190, 190, 191, 193, 195, all inside it and monotone non-decreasing. My first row OPENS ON CH 188: ep 138 (another agent's) closes on ch 187 — RQ87's ep-138 synopsis ends with the Hokuto Soke spirit deflecting Kaioh's blast and Shachi laying Kenshiro in the coffin, which is ch 187 'The Phantom Demon!!' (its cast is Kaioh / Shachi / Akashachi's corpse / Kenshiro, no Hyoh), and Akashachi is indexed 'Manga (ch. 161-186), Anime (ep. 123-138)'. My last row HANDS OFF INSIDE CH 196: ep 144 finishes ch 195 and animates ch 196's opening bedroom pages; ep 145 (another agent's) resumes inside ch 196 with the spirit above Hyoh and Lin finding the knife under the pillow. CHAPTER SPACE: the 245-chapter WSJ numbering, unchanged from the wave-6 verdict — hokuto.fandom's chapter boxes print vol 21 for ch 180-188 and vol 22 for ch 189-197, which matches our stored volume table exactly (v21: 180-188, v22: 189-197), and Coamix's own digital edition indexes the same numbers and titles (comic-zenon.com serves '第189話 ヒョウ 狂乱!!ã®å·»' at /episode/14079602755195018621). No anchor_volume_mismatch in this block. SOURCE INDEPENDENCE: three per-episode instruments were used — (1) hokuto.fandom via the MediaWiki API: 245 chapter pages carrying volume, page count, JP title and a cast list IN ORDER OF APPEARANCE, plus a per-character `appearances` field that is a two-way manga<->anime index; (2) rq87.flyingomelette.com/HNK/1/<cumulative ep>/a.html, which has a 'Manga differences' section on every row (note the path uses the CUMULATIVE episode number even though the page header calls ep 139 'Hokuto no Ken 2 episode 30' — /HNK/2/... 404s); (3) hokutosite (Shift-JIS), whose per-episode æ¼«ç”»ç‰ˆã¨ã®é•ã„ bullet lists, per-character ç™»å ´ï¼šåŽŸä½œ(N話) lines and per-arc 原作 story page (sakuhin/gensaku/hokuto/g18_syura.html) all live on ONE site served from TWO hostnames — hokutosite.com and hokutosite.sakura.ne.jp are the same site and count as ONE source. hokuto.fandom's per-chapter Summary sections are all {{Expand section}} stubs, so the chapter-level boundaries in this block rest on the cast lists' order of appearance, the chapter titles, and the two per-episode narrative sites' explicit 'in the manga X happens before Y' statements. THE REORDER ZONE (eps 140/141): the manga runs [ch 189: Kaioh and Lin; Hyoh riding with the jewels; Kaioh kills Sayaka; Hyoh arrives, is told Kenshiro did it, his matouki rises; cut to Shachi/Leia/Kenshiro by the falls] then [ch 190: Kenshiro wakes and reverses the waterfall; Sayaka's cremation; Gyoko hunts Kenshiro and dies]. The anime cuts that into [ep 140: the shelter, the revival, THEN the murder] and [ep 141: Hyoh's discovery, THEN the cremation and Gyoko], so both rows START on 189 and both END on 190 — the display shows no advance across ep 141, which is the truth of the reorder, not a gap. PACE: 8 chapters over 6 episodes (1.33/ep) against the block's ~1.8 average, because eps 139-140 are half anime-original; eps 141-144 run at the normal ~1.8. AIR DATES: RQ87's per-episode broadcast dates (Nov 12 / 19 / 26, Dec 3 / 10 / 17, 1987) match all six stored dates and all six are Thursdays, the series' slot — no date repairs.

flags_for_sean: MEDIUM, ep 140/141 — the 189/190 straddle. hokuto.fandom's cast lists put Shachi+Leia+Kenshiro at the END of ch 189 AND at the START of ch 190, i.e. the tent/waterfall sequence crosses the chapter line; no page-level source exists (the wiki's chapter Summary sections are all empty stubs). Ep 140 reaches ch 190 under either reading, because the post-revival exchange ('my wish is the same as yours — Kaioh's life') is ch 190's opening and is animated there. If a page-level check ever shows the revival is entirely ch 189's last pages, ep 140's END drops to 189 and ep 141's stays 190; the continue point (189) is unaffected either way.

MEDIUM, ep 144 — the ch-196 tail. A47 was applied: the closing bedroom scene is ch 196's opening (Kaioh's line there is cited to HnK Chapter 196 on the fandom's Kaioh page) and ep 145 continues it without re-showing, so the END is held at 195 and the tail is a `partial`. If someone counts the pages and that tail is more than five, the END is 196 and ep 145's START is 196 as well.

MEDIUM, ep 143 — the 193/194 line. The break rests on ch 194's title 'The Cold Blood Returns!' matching ep 144's opening beat (Hyoh cutting out the pressure point Kenshiro struck, which hokutosite confirms is manga content) and on ch 193 'Cold Bloodshed!' being the Kuroyasha fight. No source states the boundary in words.
